title: Start This Business With No Experience
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: The guest promotes Bridgeway Global Staffing and shares his contact details; no paid sponsorship is disclosed.

stated_problem.quote: I can't answer the phone enough. I am missing eight calls a day.
stated_problem.speaker: Alex Kirby

idea.name: Bridgeway Global Staffing
idea.one_liner: Sources and vets overseas talent for blue-collar small businesses, charging placement fees and for ongoing support.
idea.customer: Blue-collar small business owners, especially in landscaping and other trades.
idea.offer: Find, vet, and introduce overseas employees; help clients interview, onboard, and support hires.
idea.revenue_model: One-time placement fee of 28% of salary or an average $4,500–$5,200 ticket; optional $200/month support membership, with later placements at 14%.

key_quotes.quote: I should do that for the global talent that I love for blue collar focus guys.
We charge a one time fee of 28% of your one salary, or we lock it in at roughly like 45 to 5,000 bucks.
We have a channel where we have a little membership for 200 bucks a month where you get customer support, we train, we do like webinars.

acquisition_channels.details: Started by contacting business-owner friends and people in his network.
Texted business-owner friends and sent video pitches to contacts he had met on Instagram, X, and Facebook; whether recipients had opted in is unstated.
LinkedIn and Facebook/Meta ads for candidate sourcing, not customer acquisition.
Uses job boards, OnlineJobs.ph, Upwork, and Fiverr to source candidates.

ideas.delivery: Alex and his team gather the client's requirements, source and vet candidates, send a shortlist through a portal or email, arrange interviews, and help with onboarding. The client hires and pays the worker directly; the agency offers an optional support membership with training and webinars.

prices: 14% for later placements while a member

uk_legal_risk.reason: The reported customer-acquisition playbook relies on direct text and social-video messages to business-owner contacts. If UK recipients are individuals or sole traders and there is no consent or applicable soft opt-in, this creates PECR risk.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to candidate and client data, including overseas data transfers. Recruitment/work-finding may fall under the Employment Agencies Act 1973 and the Conduct of Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003. The monthly membership is described as B2B; check DMCC Act subscription requirements if offering subscriptions to consumers.

idea.name: Lawn mowing and landscaping company
idea.one_liner: Mow lawns and take landscaping jobs for homeowners and builders, earning revenue from paid service jobs and contracts.
idea.customer: Homeowners and at least one home-building company; the full customer mix is not stated.
idea.revenue_model: Paid service jobs and contracts; rates and billing terms are not stated.

key_quotes.quote: Until another pastor said, "You should start mowing lawns." So he said, "Let's give it a shot."
he did a quarter million dollars this first year and he turned it into a $2 million business

claims.claim: The host said Alex was a pastor earning about $30,000 per year before starting the business.
claims.quote: he was a pastor, newly married, making about $30,000 a year.

claims.claim: The host said Alex's wife offered to let him quit pastoring if he made $10,000 in 45 days, and said he did.
claims.quote: His wife told him, "Alex, if you can make $10,000 "in 45 days, I'll let you quit the pastor thing "and start mowing lawns."

claims.claim: The host said the business made a quarter million dollars in its first year and grew to a $2 million business.
claims.quote: he did a quarter million dollars this first year and he turned it into a $2 million business

claims.claim: Alex said he won a $30,000-per-year landscaping contract after visiting a prospect's office.
claims.quote: And he came out and we got a $30,000 year contract.

claims.claim: Alex said the prospect had responded once or twice before he visited.
claims.quote: he had responded once or twice, like yeah, I'd get back with you and stuff like that.

acquisition_channels.details: Texted friends and family with a short pitch.
Visited a home-building prospect's office after email follow-ups got no response; he falsely said he had an appointment.

ideas.delivery: Alex personally mowed lawns and handled landscaping work; the transcript also mentions a contract to mow homes under construction.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to customer contact data. Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 can apply to contracts made in a customer's home or at a distance.
